stem: Which organism is the most common bacterial cause of acute otitis media and the most common cause of its acute complications?
explanation: Streptococcus pneumoniae is the most common bacterial cause of acute otitis media and the most common cause of acute complications.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

rationale: Streptococcus pneumoniae is identified as the leading bacterial cause of acute otitis media and the most common cause of acute complications.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because Haemophilus influenzae is a common bacterial cause, but it is not the most common cause or the leading cause of acute complications.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because Moraxella catarrhalis is a recognised bacterial cause, but it is less common than Streptococcus pneumoniae.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because Streptococcus pneumoniae is the most common bacterial cause of acute otitis media and the most common cause of acute complications.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because Pseudomonas aeruginosa is more associated with chronic otitis media or otitis externa than typical acute otitis media.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because Staphylococcus aureus is not listed as a common bacterial cause of acute otitis media in this context.
